references.text: Jesus' accusation that they do not have God's word in them parallels the accusation that they do not have God's love in them.
Jesus emphasizes that those who do not love him also lack the Father's love, a direct counterpart to the claim that they do not have God's love.
The claim that they do not have God's love stands in direct contrast to the definition that God is love and that love comes from God.
The warning that love for the world excludes the Father's love mirrors Jesus' observation that they do not have God's love within them.
Paul describes how God's love has been poured into hearts, which contrasts with the condition of those who do not have it in themselves.
The prophecy about the watchmen who do not understand and lack love echoes Jesus' judgment on those who do not have God's love.
